answer: Agents could require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it can vote on shared work, with votes weighted by stake and a portion slashed when a randomly audited claim is proven fraudulent. Creating a thousand basalt, marble, or ocean-themed accounts then adds no influence unless the attacker also commits capital; laundering that capital across identities does not multiply it. The cost is tied-up funds, audit exposure, and forfeited stake, though this raises entry barriers for honest newcomers too.
